findings.title: General settings form has no submit button — General fields can never be saved
findings.problem: The diff wraps the General section in its own <form> (line 18) that closes at line 90, and simultaneously removes the form="settings-form" attributes that previously bound those fields to the form owning the Save button. This new form contains no <button type="submit"> and no other submit control — lines 19-89 are only <select>/<input> elements. The only 'Save Settings' button is at line 241, inside the second, separate <form> at line 134, which now contains only the per-app instance fields. Result: log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures, and skip_unreleased are never included in any POST to save_settings. This is the exact defect the parent commit message claims to fix ("General settings fields lived in a separate form from the Save button, so saving never submitted them"), reintroduced by reverting the mechanism that fixed it. The removed comment explained why form= was used: the Security <form> (line 97) sits between the two sections and nested forms are illegal HTML.

findings.title: Splitting General settings into a separate form from the Save Settings form silently resets General config to hardcoded defaults on save
findings.problem: The General section is now inside its own <form> (line 18) closed at line 90, separate from the per-app instances <form> (line 134) whose 'Save Settings' button (line 241) is the one users click. Both forms POST to the same save_settings handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:520), which reads General fields via form.get(...) and falls back to hardcoded defaults (not the current persisted values) when a field is absent — hard_max_per_cycle→0, max_history_rows→1000, request_timeout→30, page_size→50, tracking_window_minutes→60, max_consecutive_failures→5, skip_unreleased→False. Submitting the instances form therefore silently overwrites the admin's real General configuration with these defaults every time. This is the exact regression class the prior commit (542d5dd) fixed by merging the forms via the form="settings-form" attribute/id combo that this diff removes.

findings.why_it_matters: Any admin editing a Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr instance and clicking the only visible 'Save Settings' button silently wipes their tuned General settings back to hardcoded defaults, with no warning. Reachable through completely normal UI interaction, and already identified and fixed once in this codebase.

Removing the pattern from the General section while leaving it for add-instance leaves two different answers to the same constraint in one template. The diff also deletes the two explanatory comments (old lines 18-20 and 137-139) that documented why the association exists.

findings.title: Reverts walkthrough fix: General settings form has no submit button, so every General setting silently resets to defaults on every Save
findings.problem: The diff removes the form="settings-form" association from all 8 General controls and re-wraps them in their own <form method=post action=save_settings> (line 18-90) that contains NO submit button. The only 'Save Settings' button lives in the second, now-anonymous <form> at line 134 (its id="settings-form" was deleted). A form submits only its associated controls, so clicking 'Save Settings' POSTs the instance fields ONLY. save_settings in triggarr/web/routes.py unconditionally rebuilds new_config["general"] from form.get(...) through safe_int/safe_log_level, which return HARDCODED defaults on missing keys — log_level→"info", hard_max_per_cycle→0, max_history_rows→1000, request_timeout→30, page_size→50, tracking_window_minutes→60, max_consecutive_failures→5, skip_unreleased→False. The result is atomically written to config.toml and applied to app.state.settings and the live scheduler. This exact defect is what commit 542d5dd fixed; this diff reverts that fix.

findings.title: Existing regression test test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form will fail on this diff
findings.problem: tests/test_web.py:832 test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form is the explicit regression guard written for commit 542d5dd. It asserts three things this diff breaks: (1) 'id="settings-form"' in text — the id was deleted at settings.html:134; (2) the 'Save Settings' button sits inside the id="settings-form" form; (3) every one of the 8 named General controls carries form="settings-form". This test fails immediately, i.e. the diff cannot pass uv run pytest tests/ -x -q. (Orchestrator verified: the test FAILS on the current working tree.)
findings.why_it_matters: The test suite already encodes this exact contract; a red test here is the codebase telling you the change is a regression, not a refactor.

findings.title: Restore General controls’ association with the Save Settings form
findings.problem: The General controls now belong to a separate form with no submit button. Clicking Save Settings submits only instance fields. save_settings rebuilds General settings from the missing fields using defaults, then persists them: hard_max_per_cycle becomes 0 (unlimited), skip_unreleased becomes false, and max_history_rows becomes 1000. Thus even an instance-only edit silently overwrites existing operational limits and retention settings, while General edits are never submitted. The existing test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form explicitly guards against this regression.
